People's Majlis

People's Majlis Committee Journal

20th Meeting of the Information and Communication Technology Committee

20 October 2026

Meeting venue: People's Majlis, G (Committee Room 7)

Start time: 11:00

{Presiding: Committee Chair; Member for Milandhoo constituency Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir}

Speech from the Chair:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Assalaamu alaikum. Welcome to the Information and Communication Technology Committee of the People's Majlis. This is our 20th meeting. What we are carrying on with today is the part of studying the Digital Identity Bill by reading the draft. So, at this point I will read out today's committee attendance. Honourable Member for Maradhoo constituency Ahmed Didi, Honourable Member for Dhangethi, sorry, Honourable Member for Hithadhoo constituency Mohamed Sirhan, Honourable Member for Maduvvari constituency Ahmed Zahir, Honourable Member for North Hulhumale' constituency Hussain Shareef, Honourable Member for South Kulhudhuffushi constituency Faruhath Mohamed, Honourable Member for Makunudhoo constituency Adam Shafeeq. Thank you to all of you. So, at this point we will carry on with the part of reading and studying the draft. Thank you.

Speech from the Secretariat desk:
Authorising another party. 42 (a)- A registered party may digitally authorise another registered party, through the digital identity system, to authenticate that party's identity using that party's digital identity number and the token or authenticator linked to it, in accordance with this Act. (b)- Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section, in carrying out any transaction, the principle set out in subsection (a) of this section shall not apply in cases where a law requires a power of attorney or another legal document to be submitted to prove that an authorisation of the kind set out in subsection (a) of this section has been given. (c)- Where a registered party has given authorisation to another registered party as set out in subsection (a) of this section, unless proven otherwise, the party responsible for any act carried out in breach of this Act or any other law by improperly using the registered party's digital identity number and the token or authenticator linked to it shall be the second party authorised under subsection (a) of this section. Conditions for using digital identity. Not making the use of digital identity a condition. 43. Section 43. (a)- To obtain a service

or to access a service, this Act does not require any party to register in the digital identity system and create a digital identity. And no service provider shall compel a person seeking a service to create or use a digital identity as a condition of providing a service or of accessing a service. (b)- Even where an eligible party has registered in the digital identity system and created a digital identity, if that person so wishes, that person has the option to obtain the service by other means instead of using that person's digital identity to obtain a service. (c)- For the purpose of subsection (b) of this section, "using a person's digital identity to obtain a service" means accessing that service using that person's digital identity number and the token or authenticator linked to it. (d)- In order to achieve the objectives of subsections (a) and (b) of this section, service providers shall arrange ways by which the services they provide can be obtained without using a digital identity. (e)- Even where service providers provide a service by other means under subsection (d) of this section instead of providing the service using digital identity, they shall ensure the following. (1)- That the method set for providing that service is not one that unreasonably obstructs access to that service; and (2)- That the method set for providing that service is not one that yields a lesser or lower benefit compared with the benefit gained from obtaining the service using digital identity. (f)- Where, instead of providing a service using digital identity under subsection (d) of this section, the method set for providing that service contravenes number (1) and number (2) of subsection (e) of this section, the service provider shall be deemed to have contravened subsection (a) of this section. (g)- Where the service provided by a service provider is a service used to obtain or acquire another service, and the following are fulfilled in relation to that service, a service provider shall not be deemed to have contravened subsection (a) of this section. (1)- That a way has been made available, other than by using the registered party's digital identity, for that party to obtain or acquire the main service it wishes to obtain; and (2)- That that method is not one that unreasonably obstructs access to that service; and 3- That obtaining the service by that method is

something that yields a benefit comparable to, and not lesser or lower than, the benefit gained from obtaining the service using digital identity. (h)- Where the service provider provides the service to a party designated by a business to represent that business, or where the service provider is a party granted an exemption under subsection (i) of this section, the principle set out in subsection (a) of this section shall not apply to the service provider. (i)- Where the following are fulfilled, the Digital Service may, if a service provider requests, exempt that party from subsection (d) of this section. (1)- That the service provider is a small business; or (2)- That the service provider provides services only online; or (3)- That the service provider is a party required to provide services in special or exceptional circumstances; or (4)- That the service is not an essential basic service; or (5)- That the service provider is not a state office or an office to which Law No. 1/2014 (Right to Information Act) applies, or that the service provided by the service provider is not a service provided by the state to the public. (j)- The Digital Service shall decide to grant an exemption under subsection (i) of this section only after weighing the following and after ensuring that the exemption will not obstruct public access to that service. (1)- The obstacles that vulnerable groups among those seeking the service, in particular elderly persons or persons with disabilities or those not familiar with digital facilities, may face in obtaining the service, and the extent of the risk of those groups being left out. (2)- Whether or not the area or service for which the exemption is granted is an essential basic service, and the impact on public life or the economy if that service is interrupted; and (3)- Whether or not the service provider would have to bear a disproportionate financial or technical burden such that, if the exemption is not granted, the provision of the service by that party could come to a complete halt. (k)- The manner of applying for an exemption under subsection (i) of this section, the ways exemptions may be granted and the ways such exemptions may be revoked shall be set by the Digital Service in the regulation made under this Act. Chapter 5. Authenticating identity. Authentication facility. Section 44. (a)- In order to authenticate the identity of parties registered in the digital identity system, the Digital Service

shall establish and operate an authentication facility. (b)- In establishing and operating the authentication facility set out in subsection (a) of this section, the Digital Service shall do the following. (1)- Set the procedures, protocols and standards required to carry out authentication in the digital identity system and for service providers to use that system. (2)- Taking into account changes in technology and security matters, set the different methods of authentication in accordance with the regulation made under this Act. (3)- In accordance with international standards, set out in the regulation made under this Act and implement different identity assurance levels, from the highest level down to the lowest level; and (4)- Ensure that biometric information and biographic information are not directly linked or combined during the authentication process. Except in a situation where it is strictly necessary, where the registered party is given the relevant information in connection with the transaction for which it must be done, and after obtaining that party's consent, that information is combined or linked in connection with that transaction. Use of the authentication facility by service providers. Section 45. (a)- Service providers may request to use the authentication facility established in the digital identity system in accordance with the technical standards and procedures set out in this Act and the regulation made under this Act. (b)- The Digital Service shall set and publish clear and standardised application programming interfaces and technical protocols required for service providers to connect to the authentication facility. (c)- When authenticating the identity of a registered party using the digital identity system, the service provider shall provide the registered party with the following information. (1)- The identity information of that person that the Digital Service will share upon authentication. (2)- The ways in which the identity information obtained through authentication may be used; and (3)- Other ways in which that person's identity may be authenticated instead of authenticating that person's identity using the digital identity system. (d)- After providing the registered party with the information set out in subsection (c) of this section, the service provider shall, in the manner set in the regulation made under this Act, do the following. (1)- Obtain the consent of the registered person to proceed with authentication; and

(2)- Giving the registered party the option to give consent on condition that only certain attributes of that person are shared, or giving the opportunity to withdraw consent given by the registered party; and (3)- Maintaining logs or records of the consent given by the registered party, or of the withdrawal of that consent, or of the conditions set in giving consent. (e)- In the following situations, the service provider shall make available other ways by which a person's identity can be verified. (1)- That the party is not a person registered in the digital identity system. (2)- That the party's digital identity number and the token or authenticator linked to that number cannot be presented by that person; or (3)- That the person is unable to, or does not wish to, authenticate identity through the digital identity system. (f)- In authenticating the identity of registered parties and in obtaining information from the system's database, service providers shall comply with the procedures and conditions set out in the regulation made under this Act. Collecting information for authentication. 46 (a)- In collecting the information required to authenticate the identity of a registered party, the Digital Service shall do the following. (1)- Determine what identity information the service provider must collect, send and process in order to authenticate the identity of a registered party through the digital identity system. (2)- Determine the security and privacy-related protection measures that the service provider must establish and follow, in accordance with international standards, in collecting, sending and processing identity information for the purpose of authentication; and (3)- The manner in which identity information will be collected, sent and processed. (b)- Identity information under subsection (a) of this section shall be collected, sent or processed only to the minimum extent required by the service provider to provide that service, and in a manner that does not contravene the consent given by the registered party. Records of transactions relating to authentication. Section 47. (a)- The Digital Service shall store and maintain records of transactions relating to authentication, including the following. (1)- Requests submitted for authentication and the transactions carried out in connection with them. (2)- Metadata, including date and time records, search logs and audit trails

; and (3)- Other records relating to the authentication facility set in the regulation made under this Act, in accordance with this Act. (b)- Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section, in order to ensure that the digital identity system cannot be used to profile a registered party, or to keep watch on that party, or to track that party's activities, no information relating to the reason a registered party was authenticated shall in any circumstance be stored in the digital identity system. (c)- In situations where a law or regulation requires a service provider to establish who a particular person is or to authenticate a person's identity, if that party has authenticated a registered party's identity through the digital identity system, the records of the transaction relating to authentication may be used to prove this. And courts and the relevant offices shall accept those records as sufficient evidence to prove that the obligation has been fully discharged. (d)- The Digital Service shall keep records of transactions relating to authentication for a period of at least 5 years. And where the regulation made under this Act requires those records to be stored for a certain period even after that period, those records shall be stored in the manner set out in that regulation. (e)- Upon expiry of the period set in subsection (d) of this section, the records of transactions relating to authentication kept under that section shall be erased. (f)- Notwithstanding subsection (e) of this section, where a court has ordered the records set out in that section to be stored, or where a matter relating to that transaction has been submitted to a court or tribunal and has not been decided, that record shall be stored for that period or until that matter is concluded. (g)- In storing records of transactions relating to authentication as set out in this section, the Digital Service shall comply with internationally established standards relating to the security, integrity and confidentiality of information and the extent to which information is available, and with the relevant laws of the Maldives.

Speech from the Chair:

(After a short break) Assalaamu alaikum. We had again broken off for a vote, and at this point we will start in order to continue going ahead with studying the bill. Thank you.

Speech from the Secretariat desk:
Record keeping by service providers, Section 48. (a)- Service providers shall store the records of transactions relating to authentication carried out by a service provider, in a manner set by the Digital Service as provided in this Act and for a period set by that party. (b)- The records stored as set out in subsection (a) of this section shall not include the identity information of the registered party. However, the following information may be included in those records. (1)- The digital identity number for which authentication was requested. (2)- Information relating to the request submitted for authentication. (3)- Information received as the authentication response. (4)- A record of the information disclosed to the registered party at the time of authentication. (5)- A record showing that the registered party gave consent for authentication; and (6)- Authorisations obtained in connection with transactions carried out under Section 41 and Section 42 of this Act, and records relating to those transactions. (c)- The service provider shall not share the records stored under this section with any party other than the following parties. (1)- To the registered party at that party's request, or, where a complaint has been submitted, in connection with that, or, where a matter has been submitted to a court or tribunal, in connection with that, to the party looking into that complaint or matter; or (2)- To the Digital Service for the purpose of an audit carried out by that Service under this Act; or (3)- To state offices that have the legal power to inspect such records or that have been authorised under a court order. (d)- In keeping records under this section, the service provider shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act and the regulations made under that Act. (e)- Even where the authorisation given to a service provider to participate in the digital identity system has been temporarily suspended or revoked under number (1) of subsection (c) of Section 67 of this Act,

the obligations set out in this section relating to records of transactions relating to authentication shall apply to those parties. Access to records of transactions relating to authentication. Section 49. In accordance with the procedures and conditions set in the regulation made under this Act, every registered party has the right to obtain the records relating to transactions carried out in authenticating that party's digital identity. Chapter Six. Digital wallet. Authorising digital wallets. Section 50. (a)- The Digital Service has the discretion to authorise, in accordance with this Act and the regulation made under this Act, a digital wallet that meets the operational and technical standards set out in the regulation made under this Act. (b)- For the purpose of subsection (a) of this section, "digital wallet" means an application or system that meets the following conditions, designed for use on a personal communication device or another technological facility so as to store, manage and present a person's verifiable credentials and identity information. (1)- Having the capability, for the purpose of authenticating a person's identity, to securely store and manage that person's attributes, verifiable credentials and the tokens used for authentication, and to disclose only selected information from among the credentials and identity information stored in it; and (2)- Being something that works in a way that protects personal data, verifies the validity of identity through cryptographic facilities, and in accordance with the set technical and security standards. (c)- The regulation made by the Digital Service under subsection (a) of this section shall set at least the following. (1)- The functional, technical and interoperability standards that digital wallets must have. (2)- The situations in which a digital wallet may be used to authenticate a person in online transactions or other transactions. (3)- The measures that must be established relating to the protection of the device itself, and to prevent the information in it being obtained or changed without authorisation. (4)- The standards for accrediting parties providing digital wallets or as a party issuing verifiable credentials; and (5)- Procedures for making the changes that must be made to a credential in connection with reasons such as a change of name, or expiry, or an incident of identity fraud occurring, and in other situations,

or for transferring a credential to another system. Basic requirements that a digital wallet must fulfil. Section 51. (a)- The Digital Service shall authorise a digital wallet only after ensuring that the following basic requirements are fulfilled in that wallet. (1)- That the wallet is something that conforms to international standards, has the capability to work in conjunction with other systems, is interoperable, and is built on adequate security measures. (2)- That a consent-based information disclosure system is established in the wallet, in a way that gives the registered party the opportunity to share only selected attributes for a particular transaction, and gives the power to withdraw consent given for other transactions. (3)- That it is designed so that, where needed, a verifiable credential can be made to expire, or that credential can be revoked or temporarily suspended; and (4)- That it is designed in a transparent way in which the manner in which a verifiable credential has been used and the history of sharing can be seen, and in which the registered party can review those matters. (b)- In addition to the basic requirements set out in subsection (a) of this section, a digital wallet authorised under this Act shall fulfil the additional requirements set in the regulation made under this Act. Verifiable credentials or identity information that may be included in a digital wallet. Section 52. (a)- The Digital Service has the discretion to issue verifiable credentials that may be included in a digital wallet, in accordance with the operational and technical standards set out in this Act and the regulation made under this Act, or the discretion to authorise a third party to issue such credentials. (b)- The verifiable credentials set out in subsection (a) of this section shall be cryptographically signed, transferable from one facility to another, and compatible with the digital wallet. (c)- In accordance with the regulation made under this Act and with the consent of a party registered under the digital identity system, the following types of verifiable credentials or identity information may be included in a digital wallet. (1)- Attributes relating to the registered party that have been authorised under the digital identity system. (2)- Additional credentials issued by state offices or legal persons or other authorised parties;

and (3)- Authentication tokens or keys linked to authenticators issued under this Act. The principles relating to issuing verifiable credentials as set out in subsection (a) of this section, the principles to be followed in authorising, suspending and revoking third parties to issue credentials, and the requirements and principles that must be fulfilled in issuing credentials shall be set by the Digital Service in the regulation made under this Act. Having regard to the protection of the registered party in decisions made relating to digital wallets and verifiable credentials. Section 53. All decisions made by the Digital Service relating to digital wallets and verifiable credentials, including determining the manner in which digital wallets and the verifiable credentials used in those wallets must be designed, authorising them and the standards they must fulfil, shall be decisions made having regard to maintaining the confidentiality of the personal data of registered parties, upholding the choices given to that party, and protecting that party's safety. Status of a digital wallet. Section 54. Where a digital wallet is something used after obtaining authorisation in accordance with this Act, that wallet and the verifiable credentials used in that wallet shall be deemed valid. However, the use of a digital wallet and the verifiable credentials in that wallet shall be something a registered party chooses voluntarily without any compulsion. And the use by a registered party of a digital wallet and the verifiable credentials in it shall not become an obstacle to using other authenticators authorised under this Act. Chapter Seven. Protection of personal data. Scope of application of the Personal Data Protection Act. Section 55. (a)- The obligations and principles set out in the Personal Data Protection Act shall apply, without any exception, to the processing and procedures carried out in accordance with this Act, and to the responsibilities, duties and other matters discharged under this Act, by the following state offices, legal persons and other parties. (1)- Maldives Digital Service. (2)- Identity information providers. (3)- Service providers; and (4)- Data processors. (b)- The Maldives Digital Service and

identity information providers, service providers and data processors shall ensure the following in relation to identity information. (1)- That information is collected and processed only for a purpose set out in this Act and the regulation made under this Act, and in a manner that does not conflict with that purpose. (2)- That the information is appropriate to the purpose for which it was collected, and is not more information than required. (3)- That the information is kept for the period set in this Act or in the regulation made under this Act; and (4)- That the information is accurate, complete and up to date as set out in this Act. Situations in which processing special categories of personal data is prohibited. Section 56. (a)- Other than biometric information collected, stored, used or disclosed with the no-objection permission of an eligible party or a registered party for the purpose of registering in the digital identity system under this Act, or for the purpose of authenticating a registered party, the Digital Service, service providers and data processors shall not collect, store, use or disclose any other special category of personal data set out in the Personal Data Protection Act for the purpose of implementing this Act. (b)- The Digital Service, service providers and data processors shall disclose biometric information collected under this Act only in the following situations. (1)- To a law enforcement office under a court order issued in accordance with a law. (2)- To the registered party to whom the biometric information belongs; or (3)- For the purpose of carrying out tests relating to biometric information, conducted by storing synthetic or anonymised biometric information and in accordance with the objectives, procedures and ethical standards set in the regulation made under this Act. (c)- This Act does not prevent the Digital Service from setting, in the regulation made under this Act, the principles to be followed in collecting, using, storing, disclosing and destroying biometric information required to be collected under this Act, in a manner that ensures the confidentiality and security of biometric information, and in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act, other relevant laws and international standards. Attributes prohibited from disclosure without obtaining consent. Section 57. (a)- When authenticating a registered party's identity to a service provider through the digital

identity system, any of the following attributes relating to the registered party shall be disclosed only after obtaining the explicit consent of the registered party to disclose that attribute. (1)- Name (including former names). (2)- Current or former residential address. (3)- Date of birth. (4)- Phone number. (5)- E-mail address. (6)- That person's restricted attributes. (b)- For the purpose of subsection (a) of this section, "an attribute relating to a person" means information relating to that person, including the following information relating to a person. (This also includes information derived or generated from an attribute.) (1)- Name (including former names). (2)- Current or former residential address. (3)- Date of birth. (4)- Information indicating whether the person is alive or deceased. (5)- Phone number. (6)- E-mail address. (7)- Whether or not there is a digital identity, and the time and date the digital identity was created. (8)- Biometric information. (9)- That person's restricted attributes. (10)- The following information or opinions about that person. (i)- That person's race or ethnic origin; or (ii)- That person's political or other opinion; or (iii)- Membership of a political party or political association to which that person belongs; or (iv)- That person's religious... sorry. (iv)- That person's religious or other belief. (c)- For the purpose of number (9) of subsection (b) of this section, "a person's restricted attributes" means the following information relating to that person. (1)- That person's health information; or (2)- An identifier issued or assigned by the government, or a state office, or a foreign government, including the taxpayer identification number and, if there is a land vehicle driving licence, the number of that licence. (3)- That person's criminal record; or (4)- Membership of a professional or trade association to which that person belongs, or an opinion relating to that; or (5)- Membership of a trade union to which that person belongs, or an opinion relating to that. Prohibiting the use or disclosure of identity information. Section 58. (a)- The Digital Service, service providers and data processors shall not use or disclose the identity information of a registered party obtained through the digital identity system or through any process carried out under this Act, or such information under the control of any of those

parties, for any of the following purposes. (1)- To provide goods or a service. (2)- To advertise or promote goods or a service. (3)- To enable another party or legal person to offer to provide goods or a service. (4)- To enable another party or legal person to advertise or promote goods or a service. (5)- To use for market research or any other commercial purpose. (6)- To track or profile a registered party or to keep watch on that party. (7)- To use for the purpose of an activity carried out to convert people to a particular political view, or for the purpose of a political campaign or political activity, or for any other political purpose. (8)- For any other purpose contrary to the objectives of this Act or the Personal Data Protection Act. (b)- Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section, this Act does not prevent the personal data of registered parties collected by a service provider outside the scope of this Act from being used for commercial purposes with the consent of those parties and in accordance with the protection measures in the Personal Data Protection Act. Prohibition of tracking online transactions. Section 59. (a)- It is prohibited to use or disclose, in the following situations, any personal data of a registered party that is under the control of or has been obtained by the Digital Service, service providers and data processors, obtained through the digital identity system or through any process carried out under this Act. (1)- Where that information is personal data of the registered party; and (2)- Where that information is information relating to any of the matters below. (1)- Information on services obtained, or attempted to be obtained, by the registered party from among the services provided by a service provider. (2)- Information relating to how a registered party acted to obtain those services, or the time they were obtained. (3)- Information relating to the way used to obtain, or attempt to obtain, those services. 4- The date and time the registered party's identity was authenticated. (b)- Even where a registered party has given consent to the use or disclosure of information of the type set out in subsection (a) of this section, that information shall not be used or disclosed as set out in that subsection. (c)- This

section, notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section, the principle set out in subsection (a) of this section shall not apply in the following situations. (1)- Where this information is used or disclosed to improve the quality of, or to make it easier to use, the information technology system established by the Digital Service or the service provider or the data processor, and that is not done for a broader commercial purpose; or (2)- Where that information is used or disclosed in compliance with this Act; or (3)- Where doing so is required or authorised under a law. Situations in which disclosing personal data for the purposes of enforcement offices is prohibited. Section 60. (a)- Except in the following situations, it is prohibited to disclose to a law enforcement office, or to use for the purpose of an enforcement action of such an office, the personal data of a registered party obtained by the Digital Service or a service provider or a data processor through the digital identity system or through any process carried out under this Act. (1)- That the information is not biometric information of the registered party; and (2)- That the information is information disclosed in one of the following situations, in a manner in which the following are fulfilled. (1)- Where the information is information required in connection with a criminal offence of which the registered party is suspected, and it is established that, at the time the law enforcement office requested the information, a charge for that offence has been filed against the registered party and the trial of that matter is in progress. (2)- Where the information is information required in connection with a matter in which the registered party is suspected of contravening a law that sets a fine or administrative measure, and it is established that, at the time the law enforcement office requested the information, a charge has been filed against the registered party for contravening that law and the trial of that matter is in progress. (3)- Where the information is information that must be disclosed under a court order issued as set out in the relevant procedural or special law. (4)- Where the information is information disclosed for the purpose of reporting a digital identity fraud matter or a cyber security incident relating to digital identity. (5)- Where the information is information used to authenticate the registered party's identity with the explicit consent of the registered party. (6)- Where the information is information disclosed, with the registered party's

explicit consent, to an investigation of a criminal offence. (b)- The principle set out in subsection (a) of this section shall not apply to enforcement matters carried out under the Personal Data Protection Act by the party entrusted with the responsibility of enforcing that Act. (c)- Even where different principles relating to the disclosure of information have been set in any other law or in a regulation made under the authority of a law, the principle set out in subsection (a) of this section shall be followed in sharing information with enforcement offices. Notification of data breaches. Section 61. (a)- Where a data breach occurs that affects the security of identity information obtained by or under the control of the Digital Service, service providers and data processors under this Act, those parties shall notify the Privacy Commissioner of it as set out in the Personal Data Protection Act. (b)- Service providers and data processors shall send the Digital Service a copy of the notification made to the Privacy Commissioner under subsection (a) of this section at the time that notification is sent. Arranging privacy assurance arrangements and carrying out impact assessments. Section 62. (a)- The Digital Service shall designate a party within the Digital Service to carry out the responsibility of ensuring that, in designing and operating the digital identity system and that system's database, matters are in line with the principles, measures and standards relating to maintaining the confidentiality of personal data and implementing the security of that information as required under this Act and under the Personal Data Protection Act, and shall implement the related matters as set out in this Act and the Personal Data Protection Act. (b)- Before making any major change to the design or operation of the digital identity system or that system's database, the Digital Service shall carry out a privacy impact assessment, in accordance with international standards and principles, to weigh the impact of that change on maintaining the confidentiality of personal data. (c)- The principles relating to carrying out the impact assessment set out in subsection (b) of this section shall be set by the Privacy Commissioner and communicated to the Digital Service.

Speech from the Chair:
Yes! Thank you all for your cooperation. So, at this point we will close today's committee. Thank you.
